questions.prompt: Which principle is most useful when applying Testing Responsive Interfaces?
options: It makes every interface responsive and accessible without testing.
It runs all utility classes as JavaScript in the browser.
choose utilities that express the intended layout, constraints and responsive changes
It removes the need to understand HTML semantics, the CSS cascade or browser behavior.
questions.answer_key: choose utilities that express the intended layout, constraints and responsive changes
questions.explanation: Testing Responsive Interfaces is best understood through the syllabus topics: Browser viewport testing, Intermediate screen widths, Touch and pointer considerations. Choose the technique deliberately and verify the result.

questions.prompt: Which workflow is strongest when working with testing responsive interfaces?
options: Skip narrow-screen testing because utility-first CSS is automatically responsive.
test a narrow viewport, a wide viewport and overflowing content
Add classes until a screenshot looks acceptable without inspecting generated CSS.
Assume that starting a development server proves every page and state works.
questions.answer_key: test a narrow viewport, a wide viewport and overflowing content
questions.explanation: A reliable workflow checks generated CSS and the actual interface. Related topics include: Browser viewport testing, Intermediate screen widths, Touch and pointer considerations, Checking horizontal scrolling.

questions.prompt: Which common mistake should you avoid when applying testing responsive interfaces?
options: a desktop-only screenshot is not enough evidence of a responsive layout
Document intended behavior and test representative content.
Use the official documentation for version-specific behavior.
Check keyboard states where controls are involved.
questions.answer_key: a desktop-only screenshot is not enough evidence of a responsive layout
questions.explanation: Good styling work is verified, version-aware and tested with realistic content and input methods.
